comparisons.peer_topic: Adaptive Computing and Embedded Systems Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with the launch of Versal Series Gen 2 devices, including Versal AI Edge and Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD describe expanding or providing differentiated hardware solutions for edge computing and embedded systems in 2024. Intel highlights 'differentiated networking offerings' with features like 'networking offloads' and 'time-sensitive networking' for the 'intelligent edge.' AMD similarly states it 'expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions' including the 'Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2' which integrates AI inference for 'end-to-end acceleration.' Both companies are positioning specialized adaptive/edge processors to address specific workload requirements beyond general-purpose computing, though Intel focuses on networking offloads while AMD focuses on AI inference integration.

sentences.text: We also build differentiated networking offerings that keep pace with industry speeds and deliver unique features needed for the intelligent edge, such as networking offloads, time-sensitive networking, and scalable reliable transport.

We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.

comparisons.peer_topic: Semiconductor Solutions segment operating income drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Operating income from the semiconductor solutions segment increased, primarily driven by revenue growth from networking products (including AI networking products), partially offset by lower net revenue from broadband and server storage products.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Avago highlight networking products as a key area of growth and differentiation in 2024. Intel describes its offerings as 'differentiated networking offerings' featuring specific technologies like 'networking offloads, time-sensitive networking, and scalable reliable transport' for the intelligent edge. Similarly, Avago reports that its semiconductor solutions segment operating income was 'mainly driven by revenue growth from networking products, primarily AI networking products.' While Intel focuses on the technical features of its edge networking chips, Avago emphasizes the financial impact and specific sub-segment (AI networking) driving that revenue.
